properties.statement: [BL-207] A checksum accept now ASSERTS granularity and volatility on the author's behalf — the two properties whose whole purpose is to record what only the author can say
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-04 by watching the result of the eleven accepts in #70, which is the only place it is visible.* set_artifact_checksum returned artifacts carrying granularity: atomic and volatility: stable \u2014 properties the nodes did not have and nobody set. Measured on the merged export: exactly the 11 artifacts accepted in #70 carry them; the other 133 carry neither. ROOT CAUSE, and it is one layer down and one repo over: dynograph-core/src/schema.rs:~505 mutates the property map on validate to apply the schema default for every missing property that declares one, so every write through create_node materializes defaults for properties the node never had \u2014 the hazard graph.rs:240 already documents (\"replacing re-materializes schema defaults over everything omitted\", [BL-46]). The typed setters all rebuild the full property map and call create_node: 19 call sites across 8 modules share the shape, so this is not a set_artifact_checksum bug. WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY AND NOT AS A GENERAL GRUMBLE: set_artifact_intent's own description says these are *\"the two things only its author can say\"*, and [BL-188] exists because opaque and pending_expansion are opposite states that read identically \u2014 a decision versus unfinished work. An artifact that ought to be either now gets stamped atomic the first time anyone accepts a checksum on it, which is the exact false-green BL-188 was built to prevent, re-entering through a side door. THE RECORD IS WRONG BEFORE THE BEHAVIOUR IS \u2014 and that is why it is easy to miss: the defaults match the pre-existing behaviour (stable = any change is drift), so nothing runs differently today; only the *claim* is false. [BL-198] IS THIS, GENERALISED (*\"a serialized default is indistinguishable from a choice \u2014 28 properties carry exactly one value, 22 of them the schema's own default\"*), and [BL-46]/[BL-183] are the same mechanism in its other direction (defaults overwriting values that WERE set). The precedent for taking it seriously is already in the graph: req:mode-is-chosen-and-changeable exists because mode was *\"a governance choice asserted by a default that nobody made and nobody could revisit\"* \u2014 and its own text calls mode \"the one asserted default that is actually acted upon\", which BL-191 has now falsified, because volatility is acted upon too. FIX IS A DESIGN CALL, NOT A PATCH \u2014 three shapes, none obviously right: (a) distinguish *required-with-default* (materialize, the case dynograph's comment says it was added for) from *optional-with-default* (leave absent, apply at read) \u2014 correct, but it is a dynograph-foundation change behind a pinned v0.12.0 tag, so it crosses a repo boundary that AGENTS.md rule 6 governs; (b) reflow2-side, have setters write only what the caller supplied \u2014 blocked, since create_node is the only write path; (c) decide the defaults ARE the semantics and answer [BL-198] some other way, e.g. provenance per property value. DO NOT \"fix\" by deleting the defaults from the schema \u2014 absence behaving as stable is load-bearing. Size M", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-207 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: M."}
